unreg:all_star_week_events.blueprint_mechanism: HR is a rare per-PA event whose probability is the hitter's HR rate (barrels, pull-air, FB%) modified by the pitcher's HR vulnerability, platoon, park HR factor by handedness and weather (wind, temperature), multiplied across expected PAs and hits against starter and bullpen. Variance is intrinsic; HR/FB luck regresses. Small multiplicative shifts in environment matter because of the low base probability.

blueprint_inputs.why: Transaction timeline and rules.
Team standing drives trades: a team's playoff position and strategy determine whether it adds or sells players and thus the probability of a trade.

blueprint_inputs.why: Distribution of season totals.
Talent prior: projection systems summarise multi-year talent estimates that are better priors for team strength than early-season results.
Regress record luck: team records deviate from run-differential-based expectations because of sequencing, one-run games and bullpen luck, and deviations mean-revert.
Remaining schedule: future opponent quality, home/away split and days off shape expected wins for the remainder of the season.
Injury drag: injuries to key players and the quality of the replacement depth change a team's season-level strength.
League-level rate environment.
Run-scoring distribution for run totals.

Which stat, source and date: the settlement wording defines which events count (overtime, extra innings, shootout goals, delayed games, DNPs) and therefore changes the true probability of the same real-world sport.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes.blueprint_mechanism: End-of-season thresholds on team or league totals are determined by team strength distributions and schedule: expected wins/runs from talent estimates plus uncertainty and injuries, with regression of luck. Special markets (e.g., records, league totals) depend on rate environments and the rule regime.

Key injuries before and during the series.
Home-field and bracket structure.

Series and game price benchmark.

unreg:playoff_series_markets.blueprint_mechanism: Series probability is a dynamic program over remaining games with per-game win probabilities that depend on announced starters, rest, bullpen availability, home-field pattern and injuries. Postseason managers shorten starter leash and use best relievers more, compressing talent gaps relative to the regular season, and rotation set by off-days matters more than ratings alone.
